AccountBalanceData.description: Balance data for a single account.

balance.description: Account balance in the account's native currency (see the currency field). Its meaning depends on accountType: total account value including invested positions for Trading, Options, MoneyFarm, Spaceship and Plaee (for Plaee: cash plus the mark-to-market value of open prediction-market positions); holdings in native crypto units for Crypto; available cash for Cash. For Trading it equals equityDetails.available + equityDetails.totalUsedMargin + equityDetails.currentPNL. Not a spendable amount except on Cash accounts — see equityDetails.available.

displayBalance.description: Account balance converted to the requested display currency. Carries the same per-accountType meaning as balance, and is likewise not a spendable amount except on Cash accounts.

exchangeRate.description: Exchange rate applied to convert balance to displayCurrency.

EquityDetailsData.description: Provider-specific balance details, returned only when the request includes expand=equityDetails. All fields are nullable; only fields relevant to the account's provider are populated. Trading accounts populate available/frozenCash/currentPNL/totalUsedMargin; Crypto accounts populate cryptoId, the balance variants, fiatConversionCurrency, and orderIndex; Spaceship accounts return no equityDetails object at all; Plaee accounts populate available (withdrawable cash), frozenCash (cash reserved by resting prediction-market orders), currentPNL (unrealised profit and loss on open positions), realizedPNL (realised profit and loss of closed and settled positions, all time), invested (cost of the open positions), positionsValue (market value of the open positions), openOrdersValue (money in resting orders not yet matched), balance (cash) and totalBalance (cash plus resting orders plus open positions), all in the account currency, plus openPositionsCount (number of open positions) and hasOpenPositions (true when an open position or a resting order exists at Plaee). Currency: the fiat amounts here are denominated in the enclosing account's native currency (its currency field), not in displayCurrency — the object carries no currency marker of its own. The exception is the *InFiat crypto fields, which use fiatConversionCurrency.

available.description: Funds available to trade or withdraw (buying power); for Plaee accounts only the withdrawable cash - cash that can still be used at Plaee but not withdrawn is in balance. This is the correct field for pre-trade affordability checks — use it instead of totalBalance or displayBalance. IMPORTANT: this value is denominated in the account's native currency (the sibling currency field), NOT in displayCurrency, and no currency is stated inside equityDetails itself. Convert it before comparing against displayBalance, totalBalance, or any amount in the display currency — for example a GBP Cash account reports available in GBP while displayBalance is in USD. Populated for Trading, Options, MoneyFarm, Cash and Plaee (where it is the withdrawable cash) only; for Crypto use spendableBalanceInFiat instead, and Spaceship accounts return no equityDetails at all. For Cash accounts this equals the account's balance.

balance.description: Balance in native crypto units (Crypto); cash in the account currency (Plaee).

currentPNL.description: Current unrealized profit and loss on open positions (Trading, Plaee).

fiatConversionCurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency code used for the InFiat values (Crypto).

frozenCash.description: Cash frozen by the platform pending settlement. Already accounted for within the other figures — do not add it to balance, which is available + totalUsedMargin + currentPNL (Trading). For Plaee accounts this is the cash reserved by resting prediction-market orders.

hasOpenPositions.description: Plaee only: true when the user has something open at Plaee - an open prediction-market position or a resting order - and false when nothing is open. Absent when Plaee did not report it. Read this to decide whether to show an "open positions" state; the amounts cannot tell (a position can be worth 0).

invested.description: Plaee only: cost of the open prediction-market positions (what was paid for what is still open), in the account currency. Absent when Plaee did not report it.

openOrdersValue.description: Plaee only: money in resting prediction-market orders that have not been matched yet, in the account currency. Absent when Plaee did not report it.

openPositionsCount.description: Plaee only: number of open prediction-market positions. Resting orders are not counted - hasOpenPositions covers both. Absent when Plaee did not report it.

positionsValue.description: Plaee only: current market value of the open prediction-market positions, in the account currency. Absent when Plaee did not report it.

realizedPNL.description: Plaee only: realized profit and loss of closed and settled prediction-market positions, all time, in the account currency. Absent when Plaee did not report it.

spendableBalance.description: Spendable balance in native crypto units — not a currency amount. Use spendableBalanceInFiat for a value comparable to other accounts (Crypto).

spendableBalanceInFiat.description: Spendable balance converted to fiat, in fiatConversionCurrency. This is the correct field for affordability checks on Crypto accounts — the available field is not populated for Crypto (Crypto).

totalBalance.description: Total balance in native crypto units, including pending (Crypto); cash plus resting orders plus open positions (Plaee).

totalBalanceInFiat.description: Total balance converted to fiat, including pending (Crypto).

totalBalance.description: Sum of every included account's balance, converted to the requested display currency. Treat this as portfolio value, not spendable cash: for Trading, Options, MoneyFarm, Spaceship and Plaee it is the total account value including invested positions, and for Crypto it is the fiat value of holdings. For Trading specifically it equals equityDetails.available + equityDetails.totalUsedMargin + equityDetails.currentPNL, so it includes margin deployed in open positions and unrealized profit and loss — the available portion can be a small fraction of it. Only for Cash accounts does it equal available cash. Do not use it to decide whether a trade or withdrawal is affordable — request expand=equityDetails and read equityDetails.available (Trading, Options, MoneyFarm, Cash, Plaee) or equityDetails.spendableBalanceInFiat (Crypto). Spaceship accounts expose no spendable figure. Note that equityDetails amounts are denominated in each account's own native currency, not in displayCurrency, so they must be converted before being compared with displayBalance or totalBalance.

Possible values: `cfd`, `real`, `realFutures`, `marginTrade`. `real` - the real instrument held in full value. `realFutures` - the real future contract, which is a derivative of an underlying instrument. Each future contract usually maintains a different number of underlying instrument units than 1. The number of units held in a single future contract is called the multiplier, which can be bigger, lower, or equal to 1. `marginTrade` - the real instrument held with only a portion of its value called margin (leveraged asset). `cfd` - contract for difference, which is a derivative following the underlying instrument.

StatsRankingsApi_RankingPeriod.description:
Rolling time window over which all performance metrics are computed. Every window ends at the max date (the latest ranking refresh); examples below use a max date of 2026-07-15:
* `CurrMonth` – current month to date, from the 1st of the current month. E.g. 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `CurrQuarter` – current quarter to date, from the 1st day of the current calendar quarter. E.g. 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `CurrYear` – year to date, from January 1st of the current year. E.g. 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `LastYear` – from January 1st of the previous calendar year to the max date. E.g. 2025-01-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `LastTwoYears` – from January 1st two calendar years ago to the max date. E.g. 2024-01-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `OneMonthAgo` – rolling ~1 month window, from the 1st of the previous month. E.g. 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `TwoMonthsAgo` – rolling ~2 month window, from the 1st of the month two months ago. E.g. 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `ThreeMonthsAgo` – rolling ~3 month window, from the 1st of the month three months ago. E.g. 2026-04-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `SixMonthsAgo` – rolling ~6 month window, from the 1st of the month six months ago. E.g. 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `OneYearAgo` – rolling ~12 month window, from the 1st of the month twelve months ago. E.g. 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-15.
* `AbsOneYear` – exactly one year before the max date, with no rounding to month/year start. E.g. 2025-07-15 to 2026-07-15.
* `AbsTwoYears` – exactly two years before the max date, with no rounding. E.g. 2024-07-15 to 2026-07-15.

TradingDemoAdminApi_UnifiedOrderRequest.description: Request payload for creating an order to open or close a position.

action.description: The order action whether to open or close a position. Currently only `open` is supported in this endpoint.

additionalMargin.description: Additional funds in the order currency added to the invested amount (margin), if the desire is for the stop-loss rate to be set lower than normally permitted. Only accepted when settlementType is realFutures - supplying it for any other settlement type is rejected. Must be greater than 0.

amount.description: The monetary amount to invest in the order currency. Mutually exclusive with units and contracts. Must be greater than 0.

contracts.description: The number of contracts to trade, used for real futures instead of units. Mutually exclusive with amount and units. Only accepted when settlementType is realFutures, and must be a whole number greater than 0.

instrumentId.description: The eToro instrument identifier. For open orders provide exactly one of symbol or instrumentId - providing both is rejected.

leverage.description: The leverage multiplier to apply. Optional - defaults to 1 (no leverage) when omitted, and must be 1 or greater. Any value greater than 1 requires stopLossRate.

limitRate.description: LimitRate should be set for LimitIOC orders only, where it is required and must be greater than zero; supplying it for any other order type is rejected. it is the client submitted price which will be routed to the exchange for execution. Please note that a client submitted price cannot exceed a 10% deviation from current market price otherwise it will be rejected on pre trade

orderCurrency.description: The currency for the order amount. Typically usd. Only USD is currently supported.

orderType.description: The order execution type. Possible values: mkt (market), mit (market if touched), limitIOC. `mkt` - a market order that executes at the available market price. `mit` - a market-if-touched order that waits until the triggerRate or better is published in the market feed and then executes at the market price at that time. `limitIOC` - an immediate limit order that executes now at the limitRate or better if such a rate is available at the market, or gets cancelled immediately if no such rate is available now. `mit` is not supported when settlementType is realFutures.

positionIds.description: List of position IDs to close. Reserved for the close action, which is not supported yet - supplying any value is currently rejected.

settlementType.description: The settlement type. Possible values: cfd, real, realFutures, marginTrade. Version rules: on Public API v2 create (`POST /api/v2/trading/execution/demo/orders`, Admin v1) settlementType remains optional. On Public API v3 create (`POST /api/v3/trading/execution/demo/orders`, Admin v2) it must NOT be set for MIT orders (the platform resolves it), and for all other order types it must be set to an eligible settlement type. A mismatch is rejected during execution after the order has already been accepted with an order id. The valid values differ per instrument, direction and leverage - call `POST /api/v2/trading/info/demo/eligibility` and read `leverageConfigs[].settlementType` for the relevant combinations of `direction`, `leverage` and `settlementType` before supplying them; that configuration changes rarely, so one call can be cached and reused for the whole session. `real` - the real instrument held in full value. `realFutures` - the real future contract, which is a derivative of an underlying instrument. Each future contract usually maintains a different number of underlying instrument units than 1. The number of units held in a single future contract is called the multiplier, which can be bigger, lower, or equal to 1. `marginTrade` - the real instrument held with only a portion of its value called margin (leveraged asset). `cfd` - contract for difference, which is a derivative following the underlying instrument.

stopLossRate.description: The stop-loss rate at which the position will automatically close. Required when leverage is greater than 1, when transaction is sellShort, when settlementType is realFutures, or when stopLossType is trailing. Optional otherwise, and must be 0 or greater.

stopLossType.description: The stop-loss type. Possible values: fixed, trailing. The default is `fixed`. `fixed` - the stop-loss rate does not change. `trailing` - the stop-loss rate moves up whenever the instrument rate goes up such that the stop loss is triggered from the same distance from the last peak rate as the distance of the stop-loss rate from the rate at the open. Setting `trailing` requires stopLossRate.

symbol.description: The asset ticker symbol. For open orders provide exactly one of symbol or instrumentId - providing both is rejected.

takeProfitRate.description: The take-profit rate at which the position will automatically close. Must be 0 or greater.

transaction.description: The transaction direction: `buy` opens a long position, `sell` closes a long position, `sellShort` opens a short position, and `buyToCover` closes a short position. Currently only `buy` and `sellShort` are supported; `sell` and `buyToCover` are rejected and will be enabled in a future release alongside the `close` action.

triggerRate.description: The trigger rate for mit orders. Required for mit orders, and must be greater than zero. Must not be provided for mkt or limitIOC orders - supplying it is rejected.

units.description: The number of units to trade. Mutually exclusive with amount and contracts. Must be greater than 0.

Possible values: mkt (market), mit (market if touched), limitIOC. `mkt` - a market order that executes at the available market price. `mit` - a market-if-touched order that waits until the triggerRate or better is published in the market feed and then executes at the market price at that time. `limitIOC` - an immediate limit order that executes now at the limitRate or better if such a rate is available at the market, or gets cancelled immediately if no such rate is available now. `mit` is not supported when settlementType is realFutures.

positionIds.description: List of position IDs to close. Reserved for the close action, which is not supported yet - supplying any value is currently rejected.

settlementType.description: The settlement type. Possible values: cfd, real, realFutures, marginTrade. Version rules: on Public API v2 create (`POST /api/v2/trading/execution/orders`, Admin v1) settlementType remains optional. On Public API v3 create (`POST /api/v3/trading/execution/orders`, Admin v2) it must NOT be set for MIT orders (the platform resolves it), and for all other order types it must be set to an eligible settlement type. A mismatch is rejected during execution after the order has already been accepted with an order id. The valid values differ per instrument, direction and leverage - call `POST /api/v2/trading/info/eligibility` and read `leverageConfigs[].settlementType` for the relevant combinations of `direction`, `leverage` and `settlementType` before supplying them; that configuration changes rarely, so one call can be cached and reused for the whole session. `real` - the real instrument held in full value. `realFutures` - the real future contract, which is a derivative of an underlying instrument. Each future contract usually maintains a different number of underlying instrument units than 1. The number of units held in a single future contract is called the multiplier, which can be bigger, lower, or equal to 1. `marginTrade` - the real instrument held with only a portion of its value called margin (leveraged asset). `cfd` - contract for difference, which is a derivative following the underlying instrument.

stopLossRate.description: The stop-loss rate at which the position will automatically close. Required when leverage is greater than 1, when transaction is sellShort, when settlementType is realFutures, or when stopLossType is trailing. Optional otherwise, and must be 0 or greater.

stopLossType.description: The stop-loss type. Possible values: fixed, trailing. The default is `fixed`. `fixed` - the stop-loss rate does not change. `trailing` - the stop-loss rate moves up whenever the instrument rate goes up such that the stop loss is triggered from the same distance from the last peak rate as the distance of the stop-loss rate from the rate at the open. Setting `trailing` requires stopLossRate.

symbol.description: The asset ticker symbol. For open orders provide exactly one of symbol or instrumentId - providing both is rejected.

takeProfitRate.description: The take-profit rate at which the position will automatically close. Must be 0 or greater.

transaction.description: The transaction direction: `buy` opens a long position, `sell` closes a long position, `sellShort` opens a short position, and `buyToCover` closes a short position. Currently only `buy` and `sellShort` are supported; `sell` and `buyToCover` are rejected and will be enabled in a future release alongside the `close` action.

triggerRate.description: The trigger rate for mit orders. Required for mit orders, and must be greater than zero. Must not be provided for mkt or limitIOC orders - supplying it is rejected.

units.description: The number of units to trade. Mutually exclusive with amount and contracts. Must be greater than 0.

info.description:
eToro’s public API provides access to real-time financial data, trading insights, and account management features, allowing developers to integrate eToro’s services into their applications. With access to market prices, historical data, and social trading information, the API empowers users to enhance their trading strategies. Designed for security and scalability, the eToro API ensures smooth and reliable integration for a variety of financial applications.

For more details on integrating with eToro's public WebSocket service, please refer to the dedicated [WebSocket documentation](./websocket/websocket-doc.html).

## Authentication

Every request must be authenticated with exactly one of two options: an OAuth 2.0 access token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), or the non-interactive credential pair (`x-api-key` + `x-user-key` headers). The two options are mutually exclusive — a request carrying both is rejected. Each operation lists the OAuth scopes that grant access as alternative security requirements: a bearer token needs only ONE of them, and the same permissions govern the credential pair.

---

Full-history OHLC candles for one instrument and interval, from a public view built and kept current by a DataPlatform job. Not user-scoped: identical for every caller for the same instrument and parameters. A range without `from` returns the most recent slice; a slice covers at most 10,080 periods of the interval (7 days of 1m, up to all history for 1d/1w), and a longer range is paged with the keyset `cursor` in `pagination.nextCursor`. An instrument with no data for the interval, or one eToro shows internally only, returns 200 with an empty `results` array, not 404. Call the coverage endpoint first to find a range that has data.

Retrieve a paginated list of instruments. Any field in the Instrument response schema can be projected via the required `fields` parameter and/or used as a query-string filter (e.g. `fields=instrumentId,displayname&displayname=Bitcoin`). Use `pageSize`/`pageNumber` to paginate and `sort` to order. Filters that do not match an indexed instrument field are ignored.

parameters.description: The number of results to return per page.
parameters.name: pageSize

parameters.description: The page number to retrieve for pagination.
parameters.name: pageNumber

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. Example: pop=popularityUniques7Day,displayname
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: The field to sort by. Ascending is the default; prefix the field with `-` for descending. Sort on several fields with a comma-separated list, applied left to right (e.g. `-dailyPriceChange,weeklyPriceChange`). There is no `asc`/`desc` keyword and no space in this value - `popularityUniques7Day desc` is rejected. Not every field in the Instrument schema is sortable: unlike a filter, an unsortable or unknown sort field fails the whole request rather than being ignored.

The new secret is returned **only in this response** (one-time reveal) and can never be read again, only replaced. Nothing else about the application changes. A Market-if-touched order is an order to open a new long or short position when a specific price or better appears in the Market. The price threshold is used to trigger a Market Order. This endpoint allows traders to set up Market-if-touched orders with parameters like leverage, stop-loss, and take-profit settings. A 200 response means the order was submitted successfully, not that it was created successfully, triggered, or executed: a market-if-touched order rests until the threshold rate is reached. Confirm the outcome with GET /api/v1/trading/info/demo/orders/{orderId}, using the returned orderId.

Amount.description: The amount of the trade in the account currency [USD]. Required if AmountInUnits is not provided.

AmountInUnits.description: The number of units of the asset. Required if Amount is not provided. For most assets this can be a fractional number. Note that for Future Contracts this number should indicate the number of underlying units, and not the number of contracts, according to the formula: AmountInUnits = contract multiplier * number of contracts.

InstrumentID.description: The unique identifier of the financial instrument.

IsBuy.description: Indicates whether the order will open a long (true) or short (false) position.

IsTslEnabled.description: Indicates if a trailing stop loss (TSL) is enabled. This means that the stoploss rate indicated will get updated automatically whenever the asset price increases (for long positions) or decreases (for short position) effectively keeping the stoploss in a constant gap from the best price achieved so far.

Leverage.description: The leverage ratio for the order.

Rate.description: The trigger price at which a Market order to open the position will be sent for execution. The trigger price must be better than the current price. This means that the trigger price must be lower than current price for Long positions, and higher than current price for Short positions.

StopLossRate.description: The stop-loss trigger price at which the position will generate a Market Order to close (after it was opened). StopLoss trigger price must be worse than current price.

TakeProfitRate.description: The take-profit trigger price at which the position will generate a Market Order to close (after it has opened). TakeProfit trigger price must be better than the current price.

orderId.description: The unique identifier of the created order.

token.description: A confirmation token indicating the order creation.

200.description: Order submitted successfully. The response includes a confirmation token and the created orderId. A 200 indicates submission succeeded, not that the order was created successfully, triggered, or executed.

This endpoint allows traders to cancel a previously placed market order for close before execution. If the order has already been processed, cancellation will not be possible. A 200 response confirms the cancellation request was received, not that the order was cancelled. Confirm with GET /api/v1/trading/info/demo/close-orders/{orderId}, using the orderId of the close order you tried to cancel. If the DELETE response is lost (timeout or network error), do not resend the cancel - poll that GET endpoint with the same orderId. Units reported as executed in its positions[] array were closed before the cancel took effect; the remainder was not closed. No executed entries in positions[] means nothing was closed. Poll until statusID is terminal: 7 (CANCELED) = cancelled with nothing executed, 9 (CANCELED_PARTIALLY_FILLED) = cancelled after a partial fill (executed units in positions[]), 3 (FILLED) = fully executed before the cancel; 1, 2, 5, 6 and 11 are still pending.

A Market-if-touched order is an order to open a new long or short position when a specific price or better appears in the Market. The price threshold is used to trigger a Market Order. This endpoint allows traders to set up Market-if-touched orders with parameters like leverage, stop-loss, and take-profit settings. A 200 response means the order was submitted successfully, not that it was created successfully, triggered, or executed: a market-if-touched order rests until the threshold rate is reached. Amount.description: The amount of the trade in the account currency [USD]. Required if AmountInUnits is not provided.

AmountInUnits.description: The number of units of the asset. Required if Amount is not provided. For most assets this can be a fractional number. InstrumentID.description: The unique identifier of the financial instrument.

IsBuy.description: Indicates whether the order will open a long (true) or short (false) position.

IsTslEnabled.description: Indicates if a trailing stop loss (TSL) is enabled. Rate.description: The trigger price at which a Market order to open the position will be sent for execution. The trigger price must be better than the current price. StopLossRate.description: The stop-loss trigger price at which the position will generate a Market Order to close (after it was opened). StopLoss trigger price must be worse than current price.

TakeProfitRate.description: The take-profit trigger price at which the position will generate a Market Order to close (after it has opened). TakeProfit trigger price must be better than the current price.

This endpoint allows traders to cancel a previously placed market order for close before execution. If the order has already been processed, cancellation will not be possible. A 200 response confirms the cancellation request was received, not that the order was cancelled. Confirm with GET /api/v1/trading/info/real/close-orders/{orderId}, using the orderId of the close order you tried to cancel. If the DELETE response is lost (timeout or network error), do not resend the cancel - poll that GET endpoint with the same orderId. Units reported as executed in its positions[] array were closed before the cancel took effect; the remainder was not closed. No executed entries in positions[] means nothing was closed. Poll until statusID is terminal: 7 (CANCELED) = cancelled with nothing executed, 9 (CANCELED_PARTIALLY_FILLED) = cancelled after a partial fill (executed units in positions[]), 3 (FILLED) = fully executed before the cancel; 1, 2, 5, 6 and 11 are still pending.

Retrieves information about a close order, including its execution status and the positions that were closed as a result of the request. Use this to track the outcome of a position-closing order and identify which positions were affected. This is a read-only call and is the supported way to confirm the outcome of POST or DELETE /api/v1/trading/execution/demo/market-close-orders/... - including when the DELETE response was lost: poll this endpoint with the same close orderId instead of resending the cancel. Executed quantity is reported per affected position in positions[] (units and amount, with occurred and rate set once that position was closed); the order-level proceeds field totals what was realized. A close order that was cancelled before anything executed has no executed entries in positions[]. Any requested units that do not appear as executed in positions[] were not closed. errorCode and errorMessage are populated when processing failed.

---

This endpoint allows traders to place an order. Leverage, stop-loss, and take-profit settings can be applied. Order size must use exactly one of amount, units, or contracts. For open orders the instrument must be identified by exactly one of symbol or instrumentId - providing both is rejected. A stopLossRate is required when leverage is greater than 1, when transaction is sellShort, when settlementType is realFutures, or when stopLossType is trailing. Only the buy and sellShort transactions are currently supported. A unique X-Request-Id header (GUID) is required for idempotency. Currently only orders to open a position are supported. On this v2 create path, settlementType remains optional (stricter settlementType rules apply only on v3). A 200 response means the order was accepted for processing, not that it was executed. Confirm the outcome with GET /api/v2/trading/info/demo/orders:lookup, passing the returned orderId - or referenceId, which echoes your X-Request-Id and is the only handle you have if this response is lost. In that response, status.id 3 (Filled) and 5 (PartiallyFilled) mean the order executed; 4 (Rejected) and 10 (RejectedPartiallyFilled) carry the reason in status.errorCode and status.errorMessage; 1 (Received), 2 (Placed), 11 (WaitingForMarket) and 12 (PendingTriggeredRate) are still in flight and should be polled again. positionExecutions lists the positionId values the order produced.

post.description:
**Rate limit:** 20 requests per 60 seconds. This is a **shared quota** — the same budget is consumed by a group of related endpoints, so calling any of them reduces what is left for the others (you cannot call each at the full rate independently). Endpoints sharing this quota:
- `DELETE /api/v1/trading/execution/limit-orders/{orderId}`
- `DELETE /api/v1/trading/execution/market-close-orders/{orderId}`
- `DELETE /api/v1/trading/execution/market-open-orders/{orderId}`
- `DELETE /api/v2/trading/execution/orders/{orderId}`
- `DELETE /api/v3/trading/execution/orders/{orderId}`
- `POST /api/v1/trading/execution/limit-orders`
- `POST /api/v1/trading/execution/market-close-orders/positions/{positionId}`
- `POST /api/v1/trading/execution/market-open-orders/by-amount`
- `POST /api/v1/trading/execution/market-open-orders/by-units`
- `POST /api/v2/trading/execution/orders`

---

This endpoint allows traders to place an order. Leverage, stop-loss, and take-profit settings can be applied. Order size must use exactly one of amount, units, or contracts. For open orders the instrument must be identified by exactly one of symbol or instrumentId - providing both is rejected. A stopLossRate is required when leverage is greater than 1, when transaction is sellShort, when settlementType is realFutures, or when stopLossType is trailing. Only the buy and sellShort transactions are currently supported. A unique X-Request-Id header (GUID) is required for idempotency. Currently only orders to open a position are supported. On this v3 create path, settlementType is mandatory for non-MIT orders and must be omitted for MIT orders. A 202 response means the order was accepted for processing, not that it was executed. Confirm the outcome with GET /api/v2/trading/info/orders:lookup, passing the returned orderId - or referenceId, which echoes your X-Request-Id and is the only handle you have if this response is lost. In that response, status.id 3 (Filled) and 5 (PartiallyFilled) mean the order executed; 4 (Rejected) and 10 (RejectedPartiallyFilled) carry the reason in status.errorCode and status.errorMessage; 1 (Received), 2 (Placed), 11 (WaitingForMarket) and 12 (PendingTriggeredRate) are still in flight and should be polled again. positionExecutions lists the positionId values the order produced.

202.description: Order accepted and queued for asynchronous processing. Returns the created order details.

---

This endpoint sends a cancellation request to cancel an order before execution. An order can be cancelled if it is waiting for the market to open, or for the trigger rate to be published (MIT orders). The cancellation request may be successful, and the order is cancelled, or unsuccessful, and the order is not cancelled. This operation is idempotent when the order is already closed or cancelled. A 202 response confirms the cancellation request was accepted, not that the order was cancelled - it may already have executed. Confirm with GET /api/v2/trading/info/orders:lookup: status.id 7 (Canceled) or 9 (CanceledPartiallyFilled) means the cancellation took effect, while 6 (PendingCancel) means it is still being processed.
